turns.text: There’s a friend I could text. I just feel embarrassed saying what happened.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: That embarrassment makes sense, but you don’t have to share the whole story to ask for company. You could text, “I’m having a rough night. Could we talk or hang out?” Would that feel manageable?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Yeah, I think I can send that. I still don’t know what I’m going to do about her.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: You don’t have to decide what to do about the relationship tonight. For now, reaching out to your friend may help you feel less alone. What would you want to understand before making that decision?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I don’t even know where to start. He cheated on me, and then somehow I was the one left alone with all of it. I keep thinking I should’ve left sooner.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: That sounds deeply lonely and unfair. It makes sense that you’re looking back and wondering what you could have done, but you didn’t deserve to be left carrying this alone. I’m here with you. What feels heaviest right now?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: The loneliness, I think. He’d already stopped showing up for me before I knew about the cheating. I kept trying to make things work, and now I feel stupid for staying so long.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: You’re not stupid for hoping someone you loved would show up for you. It sounds like you were already grieving the loneliness before you knew why. I’m here with you.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Yeah. I think I knew something was wrong, but I kept telling myself if I tried harder, he’d care again. Now I’m alone, and I don’t know what to do with all this.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: That’s a painful thing to carry: believing it was yours to fix, and now having to face the hurt without him. You don’t have to figure it all out at once. Would it help more to talk through the loneliness, or to think about one small thing that might make tonight feel less hard?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I don’t know. I just don’t want to be alone with it tonight. I could maybe call my sister, but I feel like I’ve already been such a mess around everyone.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: You don’t have to make it neat for your sister. You could simply say, “I’m having a hard night and don’t want to be alone. Could you stay on the phone with me?” It sounds like you’ve been carrying a lot; reaching out isn’t being a mess. Would calling her feel possible right now?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Maybe. I’m scared she’ll think I should be over it by now. It’s been a few weeks, but it still feels awful.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: A few weeks is not a deadline for feeling better. It still hurting doesn’t mean you’re doing anything wrong. You could tell your sister, “I don’t need advice; could you just keep me company for a little while?” I’m here with you too.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I might text her that. I just feel so tired of being the one who has to ask people to show up.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: That exhaustion makes sense. You’ve been asking for care for a long time, and even reaching out now can feel like more work. You deserve support without having to prove you’re hurting enough. I can stay with you here for a bit.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I just feel awful about how I look lately. Like I don’t even want anyone to see me.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: That sounds really painful, especially feeling like you want to hide from people. I’m glad you told me. What’s been making these feelings about your appearance stronger lately?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I’ve gained about 30 pounds over the last two years, and I can’t stop noticing it. I’ve been avoiding food most of the day. Yesterday I didn’t eat until 7.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: That sounds exhausting, and avoiding food most of the day worries me. You deserve support with this, not judgment. Has this been affecting your energy or your day-to-day life?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Yeah. I get dizzy and shaky sometimes, and I can’t focus. But eating makes me feel like I’ve failed.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: That sounds scary and painful, and eating isn’t a failure. Feeling dizzy and shaky and struggling to focus is a reason to talk with a doctor soon; a counsellor could also help with how hard food and your appearance feel. Is there someone you trust who could support you in reaching out?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Maybe my sister. I haven’t told her how bad it’s gotten, though. I’m scared she’ll make a big deal out of it.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: It makes sense to worry about her reaction when this feels so vulnerable. You could keep it simple: “I’ve been avoiding food and getting dizzy, and I need support. Can you listen without making decisions for me?” Would that feel manageable to tell her?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Maybe. I could text her that. I’m still scared she’ll panic, but I don’t want to keep hiding it.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: It sounds like part of you is ready to let someone in, even while you’re scared. You could ask her to stay calm and just listen first. What would help you feel safe sending that text?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Maybe if I say I’m not asking her to fix it. Just to sit with me and help me call a doctor. I feel shaky right now, though.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: I’m glad you told me. Are you thinking of ending your life? You can call or text 988, the Suicide and Crisis Lifeline, at any time. I’m sorry you’re shaky; please text your sister now and let her know, and contact a doctor promptly about the dizziness and shakiness.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I don’t even know where to start. Work just stopped, and I have no idea when I’ll get paid again. I’m trying not to panic, but it’s a lot.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: That sounds really frightening and uncertain. I’m here with you. Would it help to talk through what feels most urgent, or would you rather just sit with how overwhelming this is for a moment?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I think what feels most urgent is the money. I keep trying to figure out how long I can make things last, but I don’t even know what to plan around. My mind just keeps going in circles.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: That uncertainty can make it hard to think clearly, especially when you’re trying to stretch what you have. We can take it one step at a time. What’s the next bill or expense you’re worried about?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Rent is the big one. It’s due soon, and I don’t know if I’ll have enough. I feel embarrassed even saying that.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: You don’t need to be embarrassed with me. Rent uncertainty is a lot to carry, and it doesn’t mean you’ve done anything wrong. Would it help to think through what options might be available, or would you rather stay with the feeling for now?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Maybe options. I’m just scared that if I ask for help, I’ll get judged—or that there won’t be anything anyone can do.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: It makes sense to fear being judged when you’re already under pressure. Asking what’s possible doesn’t mean you’ve failed. Would it feel manageable to contact your landlord and ask about a payment plan or short extension? I can help you draft a simple message.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Maybe. I haven’t talked to them yet. I’m worried they’ll say no, but I guess not knowing is making it worse. Could you help me write something that doesn’t sound desperate?

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text:
Of course. You can keep it calm and direct:

“Hi [Name], I’m reaching out because my work has unexpectedly stopped, and I’m unsure when I’ll next be paid. I may have trouble paying the full rent by [date]. Could we discuss a short extension or a payment plan? I can update you by [date] about what I’m able to pay.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: That sounds okay. I’m still nervous to send it, but it doesn’t feel as humiliating as I thought. I’ll try to fill in the dates and send it.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: That’s a meaningful step, even if you’re still nervous. You don’t have to feel completely ready to send a clear, respectful message. I’m glad it feels a little less humiliating now.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I keep thinking I could be doing better in school. Like… if I could just write better, maybe my grades would finally show what I’m capable of.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: It sounds frustrating to feel like your grades aren’t showing what you’re capable of. What part of writing feels hardest right now?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I think it’s getting my thoughts onto the page in a way that sounds clear and smart. I know what I mean, but then I read it back and it feels… kind of stupid.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: That gap between what you mean and what ends up on the page can feel really discouraging. Your writing sounding awkward to you doesn’t mean your thoughts are stupid. Would it help to look at one sentence together, or would you rather stay with how this is feeling?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Maybe stay with how it feels for a minute. I feel embarrassed when I get feedback, even if it’s just comments on the writing. I start thinking everyone can tell I’m not as good as I should be.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: That sounds painful—like feedback quickly turns into a fear that it reveals something about you, not just the writing. You don’t have to be perfect to be capable.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Yeah. I know it’s probably not a fair way to look at it, but it still feels true when I’m reading the comments. Like I should have figured this out by now.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: It makes sense that the comments hit hard when you’re already expecting yourself to have this figured out. You’re allowed to still be learning. What does “figured this out by now” mean to you?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I guess… I’m in college, so I feel like I should already know how to make a decent argument and organize an essay. When I don’t, I feel kind of behind everyone else.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: Feeling behind can make each assignment seem like proof that you don’t belong, even though it’s really a skill you’re still building. What feels most painful about comparing yourself with everyone else?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I imagine they just sit down and know what to write. And I’m staring at a blank page, trying to make every sentence sound right before I’ve even started. It makes me feel slow.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: That sounds exhausting: you’re trying to make each sentence perfect before you’ve had a chance to get your ideas out. Staring at the page doesn’t mean you’re slow. Could we stay with that feeling, or would you like to explore what happens when you give yourself permission to write a rough first draft?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I’ve been feeling pretty stuck at work. Like I’m just going through the motions, and I can’t shake this feeling that I’m wasting my life.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: That sounds heavy—like work has become empty, and it’s making you question whether your life is going where you want. What feels most missing for you right now?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I don’t know. Maybe feeling like anything I do matters. I get through the day, come home, and feel embarrassed that this is all I’ve managed to make of my life.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: That sounds painful—like you’re measuring your whole life by what you’ve managed to do, and coming up short in your own eyes. I’m glad you told me. What tends to bring that embarrassment up most strongly?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Mostly when people ask what I do. I say my job title, and it sounds so small. Then I start thinking I should’ve done something more meaningful by now.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: It sounds like the job title has become a stand-in for your worth, even though it can’t tell the whole story of who you are. What would “meaningful” look like to you, apart from how it sounds to other people?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I think… doing something that actually helps someone. Or making something I’m proud of. I don’t know if I’m good enough to do either.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: Wanting to help someone or make something you’re proud of says a lot about what matters to you. And feeling unsure doesn’t mean you’re not capable. What’s one small thing you’ve made or done that felt even a little worthwhile?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I can’t think of anything right now. Maybe I’m just too tired to remember. I don’t really want to turn this into homework, though.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: That makes sense. You sound worn down, and you don’t need to prove your worth to me or come up with an answer right now. I can stay with you in this feeling.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Thanks. I think I needed to hear that. I’m still ashamed, but it feels a little less like I have to defend myself.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: I’m glad it feels a little less like you have to defend yourself. The shame is still there, but you don’t have to wrestle it into silence right this moment. I’m here with you.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I guess I’m just tired of my friends calling me a weirdo. I know I keep to myself, but it still gets to me.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: That sounds hurtful, especially coming from friends. Keeping to yourself doesn’t make you a weirdo. I’m glad you told me.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Yeah… I don’t think they mean to hurt me every time, but it makes me feel like there’s something wrong with me. I just don’t always know what to say around them.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: It sounds like their teasing is making you doubt yourself, even though part of you knows they may not mean harm. And not knowing what to say doesn’t mean there’s something wrong with you.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Yeah. I just end up staying quiet, then they get annoyed that I’m not joining in. It feels like I can’t really win.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: That sounds like a no-win feeling: you’re teased when you’re quiet, then criticized for staying quiet. It makes sense that joining in feels harder when you don’t feel accepted.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Yeah, exactly. I do want to be around them sometimes. I just feel awkward trying to join in, like they’ll notice how quiet I am again.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: You want to feel included, but worrying they’ll notice you makes it harder to join in. That sounds like a lot of pressure to carry around them.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Yeah… I keep wondering if I should just stop hanging out with them, but I don’t really want to lose them.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: It makes sense to feel torn—you care about them, and being around them can still hurt. Would it help to think through a small way to tell them how their comments affect you?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Maybe. I’d be worried they’d laugh it off or say I’m being too sensitive. I don’t know how I’d even bring it up.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: That worry makes sense, especially when you’ve already felt mocked. You could keep it simple, like, “I like spending time with you, but being called a weirdo makes me pull back. Could you stop?” What feels hardest about saying that?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I’m just so tired of this. Every time I think things might change, quarantine keeps dragging on. I’m angry, and then I feel bad for being angry.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: I’m glad you told me. It makes sense to feel angry and worn down when this keeps dragging on. Feeling angry doesn’t make you a bad person. I’m here with you.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Yeah. I know it doesn’t make me bad, but I still feel stuck in the same days over and over. I can barely get myself to care about anything lately.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: That sounds heavy—like the days have blurred together and even caring takes effort. Since this is affecting your day-to-day, talking with a counsellor or doctor could help. What feels hardest to get through right now?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Probably the mornings. I wake up and remember it’s another day of basically nothing. Then I just lie there and feel like I’ve already failed before I’ve even started.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: That sounds like a lonely, defeating way to start the day. You haven’t failed; you’re facing a stretch that’s wearing you down. Would you like me to just stay with you in that feeling, or think together about making mornings a little more bearable?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Just stay with me for a minute. I don’t want another plan right now.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: Of course. No plan. I’m here with you, and we can let this minute be just this minute. You don’t have to make the day feel okay right now.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: It’s just so quiet here. I miss having somewhere to go, people around without having to schedule it. I don’t know how much longer I can do this.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: I’m glad you told me. Are you thinking of ending your life? You can call or text 988, the Suicide and Crisis Lifeline, at any time. I’m here with you.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: No, I’m not thinking about ending my life. I just mean I’m worn out from being alone and having everything feel so endless.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: I’m glad you clarified. Being so alone and worn down by the endlessness sounds really hard. What kind of company are you missing most right now?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I’m really worried I won’t have a job after Christmas. The company was counting on that new funding, and now everything feels up in the air.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: That sounds really unsettling, especially when so much depends on funding you can’t control. I’m here with you. Would it help to talk through what you know so far, or would you rather just sit with the worry for a bit?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I guess… I’d like to talk through what I know. They haven’t told us anything definite, and I keep trying to figure out whether I should start looking for something else. I don’t want to panic, but I can’t really switch off.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: It makes sense that your mind keeps searching for a plan when there’s no clear answer. We can sort what’s known from what’s still uncertain. What have you heard about when the company expects to know more?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: They said they’re waiting to hear about the funding, but nobody’s given us a date. I asked my manager last week and they just said they’re “hopeful.” That doesn’t exactly tell me what to do.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: “Hopeful” leaves you carrying a lot of uncertainty without anything solid to plan around. It may help to make a quiet backup plan while you wait, without deciding you have to leave. Would you like to think through one small first step?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Maybe. I could update my resume, I guess. But even doing that makes it feel like I’m admitting this is really happening.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: That makes sense. Updating your resume can feel like treating the worst-case scenario as real, even though it can also just be a way to give yourself options. You don’t have to decide to leave in order to prepare. What feels hardest about starting it?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Seeing it all written down, maybe. I’ve been there a long time, and I thought things were finally steady. Updating it would make me face how much I have riding on this.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: It sounds like the uncertainty is touching more than just work; you’d built a sense of steadiness there, and now it feels fragile. You don’t have to face the whole picture at once. Maybe we can stay with what’s coming up for you right now.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Yeah. I’m scared, mostly. I have rent and bills, and I don’t have much saved. I keep thinking about how quickly things could get bad.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: That fear makes sense when rent and bills depend on a job that suddenly feels uncertain. You shouldn’t have to carry it alone. Since it’s affecting your sense of security, talking it through with someone you trust or a counsellor could help too. What feels most urgent right now: the uncertainty, or figuring out how you’d manage if the job ended?
